Tomato.description: A popular warm-season crop that requires full sun and well-drained soil.

Plant Selection.description: Choose disease-resistant varieties suitable for your climate.
Plant Selection.tips: Consider determinate varieties for containers and indeterminate for trellising

Site Selection.description: Select a sunny location with well-drained soil.
Site Selection.tips: Avoid areas where tomatoes, peppers, or eggplants were grown recently

Field Preparation.description: Prepare soil with organic matter and ensure proper drainage.
steps: Test soil pH and amend if needed

Planting Method.description: Proper spacing and planting depth are crucial for healthy growth.
Planting Method.spacing: 24-36 inches apart in rows 3-4 feet apart
Planting Method.depth: Plant seedlings deeper than they were in pots
Planting Method.tips: Use stakes or cages at planting time to avoid damaging roots later

Irrigation Schedule.description: Consistent watering is key to preventing blossom end rot.
Irrigation Schedule.schedule: Water deeply 1-2 times per week, more in hot weather
Irrigation Schedule.method: Water at base, avoid wetting leaves
Irrigation Schedule.tips: Use drip irrigation or soaker hoses for best results

Fertilization.description: Proper nutrition ensures healthy growth and good yields.

Organic.application: Apply 2-3 inches of compost at planting

Chemical.schedule: Apply at planting and side-dress when fruits set

Weeding.description: Keep area weed-free to prevent competition and disease.
Weeding.tips: Use organic mulch like straw or grass clippings

Pest Management.description: Monitor and manage common pests using integrated methods.

Harvesting.description: Harvest at the right time for best flavor and quality.
Harvesting.signs: Fruits fully colored but still firm
Harvesting.method: Twist gently or use pruning shears
Harvesting.tips: Harvest regularly to encourage more production

Post Harvesting.description: Proper storage maintains quality and extends shelf life.
Post Harvesting.storage: Room temperature until fully ripe, then refrigerate
Post Harvesting.tips: Do not refrigerate unripe tomatoes as it affects flavor

Potato.description: A cool-season crop that produces underground tubers.

Plant Selection.description: Choose certified seed potatoes for best results.
Plant Selection.tips: Select varieties suited to your growing season length

Site Selection.description: Choose a sunny location with loose, well-drained soil.
Site Selection.tips: Avoid areas where potatoes were grown recently

Field Preparation.description: Prepare soil to ensure good tuber development.

Planting Method.description: Proper planting ensures good tuber development.
Planting Method.spacing: 12 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart
Planting Method.tips: Cut seed potatoes into pieces with at least 2 eyes each

Irrigation Schedule.description: Consistent moisture is crucial for tuber development.
Irrigation Schedule.schedule: Keep soil moist but not waterlogged

Fertilization.description: Proper nutrition ensures good tuber development.

Weeding.description: Keep area weed-free to prevent competition.
Weeding.tips: Hill soil around plants as they grow

Harvesting.description: Harvest at the right time for best quality.
Harvesting.method: Dig carefully to avoid damaging tubers

Post Harvesting.description: Proper curing and storage are essential.
Post Harvesting.curing: 2 weeks in cool, dark, well-ventilated area

Corn.description: A warm-season crop that requires full sun and fertile soil.

Plant Selection.description: Choose varieties suited to your climate.
Plant Selection.tips: Consider days to maturity and disease resistance

Site Selection.description: Select a sunny location with fertile soil.
Site Selection.tips: Corn needs full sun for optimal growth

Planting Method.description: Plant in blocks for better pollination.
Planting Method.tips: Plant in blocks rather than single rows

Fertilization.description: Proper nutrition ensures good ear development.

Chemical.schedule: Side-dress when plants are 12 inches tall

Weeding.description: Keep area weed-free, especially when young.
Weeding.tips: Be careful not to damage shallow roots

Harvesting.tips: Check for milky juice when punctured

Post Harvesting.tips: Best used within 2-3 days of harvest

Carrot.description: A cool-season root vegetable that thrives in loose, sandy soil.

Plant Selection.description: Choose varieties based on your soil type and desired shape.
Plant Selection.tips: Shorter varieties better for heavy or rocky soils

Site Selection.description: Select a sunny location with loose, stone-free soil.
Site Selection.tips: Avoid nitrogen-rich beds from previous year

Field Preparation.description: Prepare deep, loose soil for straight root development.
steps: Add sand if soil is heavy

Planting Method.description: Sow seeds directly in garden for best results.
Planting Method.spacing: 2-3 inches apart in rows 12-18 inches apart
Planting Method.tips: Mix seeds with sand for even distribution

Irrigation Schedule.description: Keep soil consistently moist for even growth.
Irrigation Schedule.method: Gentle watering to avoid washing away seeds
Irrigation Schedule.tips: Reduce watering as roots mature to prevent splitting

Fertilization.description: Moderate fertility with emphasis on phosphorus and potassium.

Weeding.description: Weed carefully to avoid disturbing shallow roots.
Weeding.tips: Use straw mulch to keep shoulders from turning green

Pest Management.description: Protect from root and foliage pests.

Harvesting.description: Harvest when roots reach desired size.
Harvesting.method: Loosen soil and pull straight up
Harvesting.tips: Harvest after rain for easier pulling

Post Harvesting.description: Proper handling preserves sweetness and texture.
Post Harvesting.storage: Remove tops and store in cool, humid place
Post Harvesting.tips: Can be left in ground with mulch in mild winters

Strawberry.description: A perennial fruit crop that produces sweet berries.

Plant Selection.description: Choose varieties suited to your climate.
Plant Selection.tips: Consider your climate and desired harvest period

Site Selection.description: Select a sunny location with well-drained soil.
Site Selection.tips: Avoid areas where strawberries were grown recently

Planting Method.spacing: 12-18 inches apart in rows 3-4 feet apart
Planting Method.depth: Plant with crown at soil level
Planting Method.tips: Remove flowers in first year for better establishment

Irrigation Schedule.schedule: Water regularly, especially during fruit development

Fertilization.description: Proper nutrition ensures good fruit production.

Chemical.schedule: Apply in early spring and after harvest

Weeding.description: Keep area weed-free to prevent competition.
Weeding.tips: Use straw mulch to keep fruit clean

Post Harvesting.tips: Do not wash until ready to use
